The most-covered record in this sample is from 2024-11-01 in Los Angeles. It is coded as Mass violence, with the actor LOS ANGELES and no second actor, and has 250 articles (Goldstein -10.0). Next is a 2024-07-24 record in San Francisco coded as Fighting, with the actor CRIMINAL and 210 articles. A 2024-08-05 Los Angeles record, coded as Fighting between LOS ANGELES and HOSPITAL, has 126 articles. A 2024-12-16 record in Beverly Hills, coded as Assault with the actor UNITED STATES, has 112 articles (Goldstein -9.0).
Two records share the actors ACTOR and TELEVISION. Both are in Hollywood and coded as Protest (Goldstein -6.5): 2024-09-10 with 110 articles and 2024-09-09 with 100 articles. Two more share the actors MARINE CORP and SAN DIEGO. Both are in San Diego and coded as Fighting: 2024-02-07 and 2024-02-08, each with 90 articles. Two records are located only as "California": 2024-01-29, coded as Fighting between STUDENT and GANG with 100 articles, and 2024-07-29, coded as Fighting between CANADA and UNITED STATES with 96 articles. Eight of the ten records score -10.0 and the other two score -9.0 and -6.5, which are Goldstein conflict scores on the coded events.
None of the records includes a Title or Summary that explains what happened beyond the actor labels and event type codes. The data therefore cannot show what any event was about, why it occurred, or who the actors were. It is also a sample of ten records and not a total or a time series, so it cannot show how much conflict there was in California in 2024 or how it changed.

results.query: Did protest activity increase in Canada this month?
results.report:
The period comparison for protest events in Canada gives this verdict: "this month is down 60.4% per day versus November 2024 (1,438 to 589 events)."
November 2024 has 1,438 events over 30 days (47.93 per day), covering 2024-11-01 to 2024-11-30. This month has 589 events over 31 days (19.0 per day), covering 2024-12-01 to 2024-12-31. The change in events per day is -60.4%. The filters are location=Canada and event_type=protest.
The two periods differ in length (30 vs 31 days), so the direction is based on events per day rather than raw totals. The comparison gives counts only. It does not show what the protests were about, where in Canada they took place, or why the daily rate differs between the two months.

results.query: Were there more protests in Texas in October than in September?

causal_candidates: The comparison is made per day because the periods have different lengths (30 vs 31 days).

results.report:
Protest events in Texas were up in October 2024 compared with September 2024. The verdict reads: "October 2024 is up 62.3% per day versus September 2024 (248 to 416 events)." The filters were location=Texas and event_type=protest.
September 2024 had 248 events over 30 days (8.27 per day), covering 2024-09-01 to 2024-09-30. October 2024 had 416 events over 31 days (13.42 per day), covering 2024-10-01 to 2024-10-31. The change in events per day is +62.3%.
The comparison is made per day because the periods have different lengths (30 vs 31 days). The data gives only these counts and rates. It does not show what the protests were about, who took part, where in Texas they happened, or why the numbers differ between the two months.

plan.thinking: The question compares two periods, so I count every matching event in September 2024 and October 2024 and compute the change deterministically instead of summarising a sample.

data.verdict: October 2024 is up 62.3% per day versus September 2024 (248 to 416 events).
